Collapsing pulse, continuous murmur below the left clavicle → PDA
Down syndrome infant with heart failure and a murmur → AVSD: echo
f: General (cyanosis, clubbing, dysmorphism, distress) · pulses (rate, rhythm, femorals) · BP · precordium: inspection, apex, thrills, heaves · auscultation · liver, lungs
Timing · site · grade (1–6) · radiation · S2 · innocent vs pathological
Wide fixed split S2 = ASD · pansystolic LLSE = VSD · continuous = PDA · ejection + single S2 + cyanosis = TOF
Tachycardia, tachypnoea, gallop, enlarged tender liver (most useful in infants)
Feel femoral pulses in every child · count the RR · check the liver
trap: Leg oedema is not an early sign of heart failure in infants · a soft murmur in a well febrile child may be innocent: re-examine
